predecessors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Egypt, 'effectively taking control of the country' after al-Adid's death in 1171

predecessors.name: Zengid dynasty
predecessors.text: Damascus (from 23 November 1174), Hama and Homs (1175), Aleppo (1182) and the Jazira cities (1182-83), taken piecemeal from Nur al-Din's Zengid heirs

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: Egypt from April 1250 (the Bahri Mamluks); Damascus and southern Syria after Ain Jalut (September 1260); Homs 1262, Kerak c.

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Aleppo, sacked by the Mongols in 1260, 'and the Ayyubids' remaining territories soon after'

ledger.x: 1171: Saladin ends the Fatimid caliphate and founds the Ayyubid state in Egypt.
1174: Turan-Shah takes Zabid and Aden for Saladin.
ledger.cp: Zabid, Aden and Sanaa (the three previous independent states; rulers not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1175: Hama and Homs fall to Saladin.

ledger.cp: Hamdanids of Sanaa (Yemen; not the Cliopatria 'Hamdanid Emirates' row)

ledger.x: 1186: Mosul bound to Saladin by treaty.
1187: Saladin destroys the crusader army at Hattin (4 July).
1192: the Treaty of Ramla ends the fighting for the Holy Land.
1229: al-Kamil surrenders Jerusalem to Frederick II.
1238: the Rasulids end Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz.
1250: the Ayyubid seat moves to Aleppo, where an-Nasir Yusuf rules the Syrian rump.
1260: the Mongols destroy the last Ayyubid state.

wars.name: Saladin's conquest of Syria and the Jazira
wars.outcome: Saladin took Damascus (1174), Hama and Homs (1175), Aleppo (1182) and the Jazira cities (1182-83); Mosul stayed Zengid by the March 1186 treaty.

wars.name: Battle of Hattin and the Ayyubid conquest of the Kingdom of Jerusalem
wars.outcome: Hattin (4 July 1187) destroyed the crusader army; Jerusalem capitulated on 2 October 1187; Tyre held out.

wars.name: Third Crusade
wars.outcome: Richard took Acre; the Treaty of Ramla (1/2 September 1192) left the Franks the coast from Tyre to Jaffa and Saladin Jerusalem, with a three-year truce.

wars.name: Sixth Crusade
wars.outcome: By the treaty of 18 February 1229 al-Kamil ceded Jerusalem (not the Temple Mount), Bethlehem, Nazareth, part of Sidon, Jaffa and Toron for a ten-year truce; Frederick entered Jerusalem on 17 March 1229.

wars.name: Rasulid independence and the loss of Yemen and Mecca
wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din Umar declared independence in 1229 and stopped the tribute; the Rasulids ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz by capturing Mecca in 1238.

wars.name: Fall of the Ayyubids in Egypt
wars.outcome: The Bahri Mamluks killed the sultan in April 1250 and the April 1253 treaty left them all of Egypt.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Syria
wars.outcome: The Mongols sacked Aleppo in 1260 and conquered the Ayyubids' remaining territories soon after; the Mamluks took Syria after Ain Jalut.

certainty.note: No survey lines: Arabian, Jazira and Nubian frontiers are approximate.
